premise: forced eviction; hidden-swap-ms not wall clock; Fresh-277 cannot exhibit contention
as_frozen_verdict: GO by the letter of 817edc7: repo+cmd_depth_4 beats cmd_depth_4 by 38.5 pp (kv=3500) and 45.7 pp (kv=5000) of the budget, far above the 15 pp bar. But see the defect below; I do not claim 'keying is the lever' on this basis.
criterion_defect: The frozen criterion compared IN-SAMPLE per-key ceilings across keys of very different cardinality without guarding against the confound. Rows per key fall from 2682 (tool_name) to 3 (repo+cmd_depth_4), and an in-sample optimal trigger on a SINGLETON group is fitted to the single row it scores, carrying zero information. The ladder therefore measures key cardinality as much as key informativeness. This is a defect in the criterion I wrote, recorded rather than repaired by moving the band.
debiased_verdict: INCONCLUSIVE. Restricting to groups of five or more rows, where in-sample fitting is least degenerate, the repo gain is 34.6% - 19.6% = 15.0 pp at kv=3500 and 35.0% - 21.1% = 13.9 pp at kv=5000. That fails the frozen 'more than 15 pp in BOTH cells' bar and lands in the 5-15 pp inconclusive range. The size_5plus restriction is itself not a clean debias, since the scored row remains in its own fit, so 15.0 and 13.9 are still optimistic.
robust_regardless: tool_name, Continuum's granularity, reaches 0.9% of the budget at kv=5000 (13.2 s of 1477.6 s) over 5 keys with ~2682 rows each. At that support the in-sample ceiling is essentially honest, so this number is NOT confounded: on this workload a tool-name key captures almost none of the available budget.
The ladder is monotone increasing across all five rungs in both cells, so finer keys do carry real information; only the magnitude at the fine end is unresolved.
Even the most optimistic fine-key ceiling, 75.0%, leaves a quarter of the budget beyond any per-key method.
